The largest number of defective units in the sample that still allows the lot to be accepted.
The quality level at which a sampling plan accepts a lot with high probability when the supplier's process runs at that average.
How close the commanded placement position is to the true board location.

The radial gap between the finished hole wall and the lead.
The width of copper remaining around a drilled hole after plating.

A fixture with spring-loaded probes that contact all test points at once.
A distribution with two peaks, showing that two different populations are being measured together.

The formation and collapse of vapour bubbles in a liquid that dislodges contamination.

Supplier declaration that a lot meets the purchase order and the referenced acceptance criteria; it is evidence of declared conformity, not of inspection by the buyer.

A structured exercise in naming defect type and disposition from images.

Bending the protruding lead to hold the component during handling and soldering.
The controlled temperature path a material follows from manufacture through storage and transport to use.

The reduction in BGA ball height during reflow as the ball settles onto the land.

A written approval to use material that does not meet the stated requirement.
An observable state that may or may not be a defect depending on the class and criteria applied.
A copper filament that grows through laminate along glass fibres under bias and moisture.
The resistance added by the probe-to-pad interface, which must stay low and stable.
The interval a board spends in contact with the solder wave.
Immediate action to stop nonconforming material from moving further into the process or to the customer.
The document stating what is measured, how often, against what limit, and the reaction when it fails.
How well the leads or terminations of a component lie in one plane.
The cost of scrap, rework, inspection and lost capacity caused by defects.
A part whose identity, grade or origin is misrepresented, including re-marked, refurbished or unauthorised copies.
The specification width divided by six standard deviations, a measure of spread alone.
The distance from the mean to the nearer specification limit in standard deviations, a measure of spread and centring.
The height of the solder wave above the nozzle opening.
The total time a package has spent above 90 °C, limited because solderability degrades with it.
The total time a device has spent outside a compliant moisture barrier bag since its last valid reset.

Design change request, the engineering request that initiates a change before formal approval.
The fraction of expected defect modes a method can detect, weighted by occurrence.
Defects normalised to board area or joint count, allowing comparison across sizes.
A defect rate normalised by the number of countable opportunities in the product.

A measurable constraint applied during layout or stencil design.
A drawing, layer, dimension or library attribute the designer controls.
A defect that passed the inspection or test intended to catch it.
The smallest value an analytical method can report as distinguishable from background.
The likelihood that a method reports a present defect of a given class.

Hole diameter minus lead diameter at the joint.
The area under the die where the package mass changes heat flow and paste behaviour.
A second review of a sample of dispositions to test consistency.
The recorded decision on a nonconforming item: accept, reject, rework, repair, scrap or use-as-is.

A stated allowance in the standard that permits a lower value under defined conditions.

The gap between the component body and the board surface.

formulas.name: Area ratio (stencil aperture)
formulas.where: release capability of a rectangular aperture; L and W are the aperture sides, T the foil thickness
formulas.lessonTitle: The paste volume budget: what the joint needs before the aperture is drawn
formulas.quote: Area ratio is the aperture area divided by the sidewall area of the stencil wall.
formulas.heading: Area ratio compares contact area with wall adhesion

formulas.name: Aspect ratio (stencil aperture)
formulas.where: release capability on the narrow side; W is aperture width, T the foil thickness
formulas.lessonTitle: The paste volume budget: what the joint needs before the aperture is drawn
formulas.quote: Aspect ratio is aperture width divided by stencil thickness, and for rectangular apertures you take the smaller dimension, because that dimension controls the narrowest release path.
formulas.heading: Aspect ratio describes depth against width

formulas.name: Squeegee pressure per blade length
formulas.where: pressure in N/mm; F is the force applied to the blade, L the blade length
formulas.lessonTitle: Printer setup: squeegee pressure and speed, snap-off, separation, wipe cycle
formulas.quote: Industry guidance clusters around 0.45 to 0.70 kg per 25 mm of blade, which is 0.2 to 0.6 N/mm; work in N/mm and state the blade length with every setting, because 0.2 N/mm on a 250 mm blade is 50 N and 0.6 N/mm is 150 N.
formulas.heading: Squeegee pressure

formulas.name: Process capability index
formulas.where: capability of a stable process against its specification limits
formulas.lessonTitle: SPI as process evidence: mean, spread, capability, stop/adjust decisions
formulas.quote: Cpk adds centring — whether it actually is centred enough to meet them.
formulas.heading: Capability for volume and height

formulas.name: Wave contact time from contact length
formulas.where: dwell over the wave; L is the effective contact length, v the conveyor speed
formulas.lessonTitle: Contact time and fog height: dwell calculation, wave height vs board clearance
formulas.quote: Calculate it as t = L / v, where L is the effective contact length in mm and v the conveyor speed in mm/s.
formulas.heading: Contact time and why it matters

formulas.name: Shadow length behind a lifted lead
formulas.where: the wake a tall part casts in the wave, plus a turbulence margin
formulas.lessonTitle: Shadowing and orientation: shading, pallets, board direction, lead geometry
formulas.quote: Board direction changes the shadow length, because the same component presents a different projected height to the wave.
formulas.heading: Board and wave direction

formulas.name: Thermal budget index for hand rework
formulas.expr: index = (tip setpoint − board preheat) × contact time
formulas.where: a comparable number for one rework contact, in °C·s
formulas.lessonTitle: Technique: contact order, dwell, feed, lead-free discipline, technique defects
formulas.quote: State thermal budget: tip setpoint 330-350 °C, board preheat 100 °C, contact time 1.5-2.5 s, initial contact; thermal budget index = (tip setpoint - board preheat) × contact time = 230-250 °C × 1.5-2.5 s = 345-625 °C·s per contact.
formulas.heading: Worked calculation

formulas.name: Estimated dry-film thickness from wet film
formulas.where: coating thickness after cure; WFT is the measured wet film, solids given as a fraction
formulas.lessonTitle: Application and masking: spray, dip, selective, thickness, cure, repairability
formulas.quote: The coating has a volume solids content of 45% by volume.
formulas.heading: Worked calculation

formulas.name: Defect rate in parts per million
formulas.where: defect rate normalised by the opportunity count the report states
formulas.lessonTitle: Coverage math: node vs defect coverage, escape risk, where inspection ends and test starts
formulas.quote: Use SI units such as millimetre and micrometre for physical inspection limits, and ppm as the dimensionless rate for escape risk.
formulas.heading: Coverage math needs a defect model

formulas.name: Escape count from a defect rate
formulas.where: how many defective units reach the next stage at a stated rate
formulas.lessonTitle: Containment and traceability: quarantine scope, lot trace, retroactive search
formulas.quote: Measure effectiveness with a metric tied to the defect: solder defect ppm, first pass yield, rework rate, test escape rate or audit findings.
formulas.heading: Owners, dates and effectiveness metrics

formulas.name: Sample size for a no-defect demonstration
formulas.where: units needed to show a defect rate p with no defect found
formulas.lessonTitle: How designers read process feedback: language, format, what gets acted on
formulas.quote: With confidence = 0.95 and target = 0.0010, n = ln(0.05) / ln(0.999) = 2995.
formulas.heading: Worked calculation
